title: Director of Quality, Infection Prevention, Regulatory & Accreditation HRC-210
text:
**Position Summary**

Directs the Infection Prevention (IP) Program within San Benito Health Care District (SBHCD) to ensure compliance with TJC, State and CMS regulations. Works in collaboration with hospital leaders to plan, coordinate, and evaluate IP program, policies and activities. Updates annual IP risk assessment and IP Plan with environmental, programmatic, facility, and/or regulatory changes. Provides expert consultation and education to minimize healthcare-associated infections and transmission among patients, staff, providers, and visitors. In addition, they will oversee the activity of regulatory and accreditation throughout the district. Responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining a system of regulatory and reliability testing for the organization’s products and/or development processes and ensure survey readiness for surveys. Leads the organization’s Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) and patient safety programs across the hospital, skilled nursing facilities, clinics, and ambulatory surgery center. Provides strategic leadership for organization-wide quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability initiatives. Promotes a culture of safety, continuous improvement, accountability, and high-quality patient care through data analysis, performance improvement, and collaboration with clinical, medical staff, and operational leaders.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Conducts ongoing surveillance for detection of nosocomial infections.
* Systematically collects data for the purpose of identifying and tracking high-risk/volume hospital-acquired infections (HAI) and sources of infection.
* Recommends, monitors, and evaluates effectiveness of appropriate IP interventions.
* Collaborates with the hospital and physician leaders to coordinate the IP program to design & implement strategies and interventions to decrease the impact of nosocomial infections across the continuum of car.
* Analyzes IP surveillance data and ensures communicable diseases and HAI are reported internally and externally (County, State, NHSN-CDC) as required.
* Monitors for breaks in asepsis and potential sources of infections; coordinates effective outbreak detection and resolution.
* Reviews patient medical records and other pertinent clinical data.
* Assures compliance with isolation practices and policies.
* Provides orientation and ongoing education to staff and providers.
* Creates and updates IP Policies to keep information and practices current.
* Oversees the hand hygiene program to minimize transmission of HAI.
* Coordinates the IP Committee to review IP data, plans, and policies within specified timeframes.
* Updates the IP Plan and risk assessment annually.
* Participates with environmental rounds team and presents quarterly IP reports for Safety Committee.
* Promotes employee growth and development through effective use of resources, internally and externally.
* Oversees direct operations, including staff and budget, of the following areas: QAPI / Patient Safety, Accreditation (TJC), Regulatory Compliance (CDPH, CMS).
* Organizes coordinates and attends all hospital, board quality, and Medical Staff committee meetings and participates in all pertinent hospital committee meetings where monitoring functions and activities are performed.
* Ensures compliance with TJC, CDPH & CMS regulations.
* Survey readiness, and Plan of Correction follow up.
* Regulatory reporting & Follow up.
* Oversees regulatory readiness, quality measurement, public reporting, and pay-for-performance programs and initiatives, holding staff and departments accountable for achieving performance goals.
* Establishes measurement and improvement activities, including methods to track implementation of action plans following site surveys and critical events reviews.
* Coordinates and manages Core Measures reporting and other functions.
* Leads the root cause analyses and failure modes and effects analyses and debriefings.
* Promotes a culture of safety, high reliability, patient and staff engagement, and performance excellence.
* Develops, evaluates, and maintains dashboards and performance metrics.
* Implementing, monitoring and updating organization’s compliance plan.
* Monitoring and auditing functions of the compliance plan.
* Develops, implements, evaluates, and maintains the organization-wide QAPI and patient safety programs in alignment with organizational priorities and applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements.
* Leads quality improvement and performance improvement initiatives focused on clinical outcomes, patient safety, efficiency, patient experience, and reliability of care.
* Collects, analyzes, trends, and reports quality and patient safety data to identify opportunities for improvement and evaluate the effectiveness of corrective actions and improvement initiatives.
* Oversees the identification, review, investigation, and analysis of adverse events, near misses, patient safety concerns, and other quality-of-care issues, as appropriate.
* Leads or facilitates Root Cause Analyses (RCA), Failure Modes and Effects Analyses (FMEA), and other structured performance improvement methodologies.
* Develops and maintains quality dashboards, key performance indicators, benchmarks, and other performance measures used to monitor organizational and departmental performance.
* Collaborates with physicians, Medical Staff leadership, nursing leadership, department leaders, and frontline staff to implement evidence-based practices and organization-wide performance improvement initiatives.
* Monitors quality performance across hospital, skilled nursing facility, clinic, and ambulatory surgery center services and works with department leaders to address identified gaps.
* Coordinates and supports applicable quality reporting, including Core Measures, public reporting, regulatory quality measures, and pay-for-performance initiatives.
* Prepares and presents quality, QAPI, and patient safety reports to executive leadership, the Board of Directors, Medical Staff, and applicable quality and patient safety committees.
* Supports Medical Staff quality activities, including peer review processes and ongoing and focused professional practice evaluation (OPPE/FPPE), as applicable.
* Establishes processes to monitor corrective action plans and performance improvement activities resulting from regulatory surveys, quality reviews, adverse event investigations, and identified performance gaps.
* Promotes a culture of safety, high reliability, continuous improvement, transparency, accountability, and patient-centered care throughout the organization.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree(Engineering, Microbiology, Nursing, Public Health, Epidemiology, or other Healthcare related field) required; Master degree in either Microbiology, Nursing, Public Health, Epidemiology, or other Healthcare related field preferred.
* Minimum of 2-5 years’ experience in infection prevention, quality management, and/or regulatory compliance, including nursing, epidemiology public health or related field required.
* Minimum of 5 years of Director level experience.
* Board Certification in Infection Prevention and Control required.
* Experience with emergency management, disaster preparedness and/or hazardous materials management.

**Job Type:** Full-time, Day Shift

**Pay:** $225K-$250K/annually

All job offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, physical exam, drug test, and verification of education qualifications and credentials.
